title: Probing hydrodynamics in graphene and quark matter via Seebeck coefficient
authors: Subhalaxmi Nayak, Jayanta Dey, Sabyasachi Ghosh
abstract: We investigate the Seebeck coefficient as a probe of collective transport behavior in graphene and quark-gluon plasma using a kinetic-theory approach in the hydrodynamic regime. The Seebeck coefficient is obtained by solving the Boltzmann transport equation in the relaxation-time approximation. At high-charge-carrier density, corresponding to the Fermi-liquid domain, our result approaches the behavior expected from the conventional Mott relation. In contrast, significant deviations from the Mott relation are observed in the low-carrier-density regime, corresponding to the Dirac fluid domain. These facts are in good agreement with experimental Seebeck coefficient data for graphene. This behavior indicates the emergence of collective hydrodynamic transport in graphene. The enthalpy per particle plays a key role for the Seebeck coefficient in the Dirac fluid regime. We extend our formalism to the ultra-relativistic quark-gluon plasma. A similar deviation from the Mott relation is observed, supporting a similar fluid response in the Seebeck coefficient across two markedly different strongly correlated quantum systems - graphene and quark matter.
summary: This work uses the Seebeck coefficient to study hydrodynamic transport in graphene and quark matter. By solving the Boltzmann transport equation, the authors show that deviations from the standard Mott relation in the low-density regime confirm the presence of collective fluid behavior in both systems. This provides a unified theoretical framework for understanding transport in different strongly correlated quantum materials.
main_problem: The paper investigates the Seebeck coefficient as a diagnostic tool to probe collective hydrodynamic transport behavior in strongly correlated quantum systems like graphene and quark-gluon plasma.
main_result: The Seebeck coefficient deviates significantly from the conventional Mott relation in the low-carrier-density (Dirac fluid) regime for both graphene and QGP, indicating the emergence of collective hydrodynamic transport.
method: The study employs a kinetic-theory approach, solving the Boltzmann transport equation in the relaxation-time approximation (RTA) to derive transport coefficients.
model_or_system: The primary systems are graphene (a 2D Dirac fermion system) and the quark-gluon plasma (QGP). The analysis treats these systems using a quasi-relativistic fluid model derived from conservation laws.
key_observables: Seebeck coefficient (S), electrical conductivity ($\sigma_e$), and thermal conductivity ($\kappa_e$).
important_parameters: Carrier density ($n$), chemical potential ($\mu$), and temperature ($T$). Key regimes include the Fermi-liquid (FL) and Dirac fluid (DF) domains.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the relaxation-time approximation (RTA) and assumes an energy-independent relaxation time to satisfy conservation laws.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate thermodynamic quantities (density vs. chemical potential) and plot transport coefficients ($\sigma_e$ and $\kappa_e$) versus carrier density for graphene.
paper_structure: The paper derives the Seebeck coefficient for both graphene and QGP using the BTE in RTA, comparing the results against the Mott relation across different carrier density regimes.
why_interesting: The connection between macroscopic transport coefficients (like S) and underlying fluid dynamics in exotic quantum matter (like graphene or QGP) provides insights into non-equilibrium many-body physics, which is relevant to understanding strongly interacting quantum systems.
